record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two, where “non-special” means that P is neither a Lattès map nor conjugate to z^±n or ±T_n for some n ≥ 2. Let C(P) be the semigroup of rational functions commuting with P, and let G_P be the finite quotient group obtained from C(P) by identifying Q_1 and Q_2 whenever Q_1∘P^{∘l_1} = Q_2∘P^{∘l_2} for some l_1, l_2 ≥ 0. Which finite groups can occur as G_P?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a rational function on the Riemann sphere of degree at least two. Call $P$ special if it is either a Lattès map (i.e., a rational function arising as a quotient of an endomorphism of an elliptic curve by a finite automorphism group), or conjugate via a Möbius transformation to $z\mapsto z^n$, $z\mapsto z^{-n}$, $z\mapsto T_n(z)$, or $z\mapsto -T_n(z)$ for some integer $n\ge 2$, where $T_n$ denotes the $n$-th Chebyshev polynomial. Otherwise, call $P$ non-special.

For a rational function $P$ of degree $\ge 2$, let
$$C(P) = \{Q\in\mathbb{C}(z) : Q\circ P = P\circ Q\}$$
be the semigroup (under composition) of rational functions commuting with $P$. Define an equivalence relation $\sim_P$ on $C(P)$ by declaring $Q_1 \sim_P Q_2$ if there exist non-negative integers $l_1, l_2$ such that
$$Q_1 \circ P^{\circ l_1} = Q_2 \circ P^{\circ l_2},$$
where $P^{\circ l}$ denotes the $l$-fold compositional iterate of $P$ (with $P^{\circ 0} = z$). When $P$ is non-special, $\sim_P$ is a congruence on $C(P)$ and the quotient $G_P := C(P)/\!\sim_P$ is a finite group.

Determine which finite groups $G$ arise as $G_P$ for some non-special rational function $P$ of degree at least two.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed by Pakovich as an open problem: while $G_P$ is shown to be a finite group with generators describable via the fundamental group of an associated graph, no classification of the finite groups arising as $G_P$ has been established. Subsequent works on commuting rational functions and amenable/tame semigroups continue to study $C(P)$ but do not announce a resolution of the realization question.

status_evidence.title: Commuting rational functions revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Defines an equivalence relation on rational functions commuting with B such that the quotient is a finite group G_B, with generators described via a fundamental group of an associated graph.
status_evidence.claim: G_P is a finite group whose structure is described, but the realization problem (which finite groups occur) is left open.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions (Pakovich)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies subsemigroups of C(P) for non-special rational functions P of degree at least two; uses the finite group structure without classifying the groups G_P.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work uses G_P but does not classify which finite groups occur.
